Team —

Quick sync ask for this week: Acme (ACME-5421) is moving faster than we expected and Sales wants a clear recommendation on whether to propose a Dedicated pool commitment or a short-term burst plan. I attached the deal velocity snapshot from yesterday for context.

Two asks:
1) Sales/LAURA — can you call out which deals in the attached snapshot are most likely to convert in the next 30/60/90 days and estimate committed GPU slot equivalents (p50)?
2) Infra/MARCUS — give two sizing options for Acme (conservative + aggressive) with lead-time risk and whether we can satisfy with burst slots vs reserved capacity. Include any preemption or performance caveats.
3) Finance/BEN — high-level run-rate delta (monthly cost) for the two options so we can feed that into the commercial proposal.

I want to collect input by EOD Thu (Jun 3) and publish a short recommendation for the account review on Tue. If anything here needs a separate deep-dive, flag it and we’ll schedule.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pool projection & deal velocity check — week of Jun 2

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the ask. Summary of infra view (today's utilization and two scenarios attached):

Current state:
- Pool utilization: 68% average across reserved fleets; burst headroom at ~22% under current config.
- Lead time for adding reserved racks (procurement + build + QA): ~6–8 weeks.

Option A (Conservative / Burst-first):
- Keep current reserved capacity, provide predictable burst slots for initial onboarding (~8–12 slots sustained for 6–8 weeks).
- Pros: fastest, lower upfront commitment, avoids rebalancing.
- Cons: higher per-token cost during heavy QPS; may hit burst throttles if traffic spikes.

Option B (Aggressive / Reserve 40 slots):
- Procure and reserve 40 slots; schedule provisioning with net-new reserved capacity in 6–8 weeks.
- Pros: lower unit cost, stable latency, easier SLO guarantees for committed workloads.
- Cons: capital commitment, possible underutilization if ACME scales slower.

I attached a quick scenario workbook — pool_scenarios_20270602.xlsx — that models latency vs cost for both options (assumes 2.4k tokens/day per active user and a 75th percentile seq-length of 128 tokens).

If Sales thinks ACME needs SLAs for inference latency starting day one of production, Option B is the recommendation. If they can accept a short period on burst capacity and SLOs with throttling, we should run Option A and re-evaluate once usage stabilizes.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 3, 2027 at 8:40 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Pool projection & deal velocity check — week of Jun 2

Team —

High-level finance impact (back-of-envelope):
- Option A (burst): incremental monthly cost ~ $28k — covers burst credits and short-term autoscaling premium.
- Option B (reserve 40 slots): effective monthly run-rate ~ $18k after capitalized reservation amortization (assuming annual commit).

Key asks for a clean commercial recommendation:
1) Confirm expected committed slot count (p50) and whether the customer will sign an annual or quarterly commit.
2) Confirm when they need production-grade SLAs (immediate vs after 6–8 weeks).
3) Any special billing terms or discounts requested by Acme (I saw a note about a potential 10% TCV discount in the CRM).

If Sales confirms ACME-5421 will go annual for 40 slots, finance can model the exact amortization and present an MRR delta for the account review. Otherwise, we should default to Option A and include a clause for transitioning to reserved at month+3.

—Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — good input. Final notes and next steps: 

Decisions:
- Recommend to Acme: start on Option A (burst) for onboarding with an explicit conversion trigger at month 3 to reserve 40 slots if usage meets the p50 threshold. This reduces lead-time risk and keeps commercial flexibility.
- If Acme requests production SLAs before week 6, we’ll escalate to provision reserved capacity earlier and finance will surface revised MRR impact.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Laura: confirm ACME-5421 commit horizon (annual vs quarterly) and update HubSpot by EOD Mon (Jun 7).
- Marcus: prepare a light playbook for burst-to-reserve transition (ops runbook + perf caveats) by Jun 9. Attach to the Drive folder.
- Ben: draft the MRR/commit amortization slide for Tuesday account review; include the 10% discount scenario.

I've looped in Sarah at Acme to confirm they are comfortable with a burst-first approach and the conversion trigger. Sarah — quick Q: would Acme agree to a 3-month evaluation window that defaults to reserved commit if usage thresholds are met? Reply OK and we’ll include in the commercial term sheet.

Related links/attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_pool_planning | DocuSign link will follow once terms are agreed.
